verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents a public Management API with an OpenAPI 3.0 reference. The API covers workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions, and the vendor says its CLI "does everything the UI does." An MCP server also exposes pipeline management and Live Events to agents. The probe could not find the OpenAPI spec at common paths, but it did not check the stated docs.jitsu.com/api location, so this lowers confidence rather than contradicting the claim. missing for 10: an explicit parity statement for the API itself rather than the CLI, a fetchable machine-readable OpenAPI spec, independent or hands-on confirmation of UI parity

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: A public Management API for every Jitsu instance, with a full OpenAPI 3.0 reference at docs.jitsu.com/api. jitsu-cli — a real command-line interface that does everything the UI does.
Jitsu exposes an HTTP API for managing workspaces, sites, destinations, connections, syncs and functions.
Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.
